questions.q: Which formula does the chapter's tiering engine use for a relation's heat score?
options: log_bytes / (rows_modified + 1)
avg_stall_ms / io_ops
waste ratio = (page_count * 8KB) / (record_count * avg_record_size)
heat_score = (reads_per_hour * 0.4) + (writes_per_hour * 0.5) + (1 / days_since_modified * 0.1)
questions.explain: The heat score weights reads at 0.4, writes at 0.5, and recency of modification at 0.1; cold relations are demoted and hot relations on slow tiers are promoted.

questions.q: When checkpoint I/O dominates total write I/O during burst windows and average write stall is high, what is the autonomous checkpoint controller's correct response?
options: Raise TARGET_RECOVERY_TIME to spread dirty-page flushes over a longer interval
Lower TARGET_RECOVERY_TIME to fire checkpoints more often
Enable DELAYED_DURABILITY = FORCED
Rebuild all indexes on the log device
questions.explain: Raising TARGET_RECOVERY_TIME spreads dirty-page flushes over a longer interval, trading a bounded increase in recovery time for smoother I/O; it is lowered when dirty pages accumulate faster than checkpoints drain.

questions.q: Per the chapter, what remediation is recommended when sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats reports avg_fragmentation_in_percent > 30?
options: REORGANIZE
Nothing until 50%
REBUILD
Drop and recreate the index
questions.explain: Above 30% fragmentation the recommendation is REBUILD; between 10% and 30% it is REORGANIZE; REORGANIZE is the first-line response for compacting pages and reclaiming ghost records.

questions.q: What safety interlock gates the autonomous bloat remediation system before it runs an online index rebuild?
options: It requires a full backup within the last hour
It waits if any data device exceeds 70% iostat utilization, with exponential backoff up to 4 hours before escalating
It pauses until the buffer pool is flushed
It disables Resource Governor for the session
questions.explain: The interlock prevents remediation from becoming its own source of I/O saturation: if any data device is over 70% utilized, the agent backs off exponentially for up to 4 hours, then escalates.

questions.q: What is the chapter's policy on DELAYED_DURABILITY = FORCED?
options: Enable it for all non-critical workloads
Never set it without explicit operator permission (allow_forced = False), since it sacrifices crash safety
Use it as the default during checkpoint storms
Apply it to tempdb only
questions.explain: The policy flag allows delayed durability (ALLOWED) for non-critical workloads under WRITELOG pressure but never FORCED, because that sacrifices crash safety without human approval.
